deviations_from_adr: ADR-T0612 is a SERVER/linter+fix-artifact ADR; T-0660 is its UI-modeler complement. No deviation from the ADR's decisions (D1 non-interrupting=reminder, D2 converging exclusiveGateway) — the canvas affordance builds exactly the D2 converging shape the ADR mandates and the T-0641/T-0612 linter enforces.
cancelActivity is written as the NATIVE BPMN attribute (not a choros:* extension) because Flowable reads it directly — no server mapper change needed, keeping strictly within the web/ boundary.

U-1 (design-steward, fixed): the build was ~8 separate modeling commands (undo required ~8 Ctrl+Z). Now ONE composite command choros.escalationBranch.build (canonical diagram-js AppendShapeHandler pattern: nested modeling ops in preExecute share the base action id; CommandStack.undo/redo loop while ids match) — one click = ONE undo entry. Pinned on a LIVE bpmn-js Modeler (real CommandStack) in escalation-branch-undo.test.js; mutation-proven RED (direct-modeling bypass → both undo tests fail).

bpmn-auto-layout@1.3.0 emits BPMNShape geometry for the built nodes but NO BPMNEdge waypoints for this boundary+convergence topology; edge DI is generated by the LIVE bpmn-js modeling API (appendShape/connect) in the product. DI test asserts node shapes + clean bpmn-moddle re-import; the undo test now ALSO exercises the live modeling API end-to-end (real Modeler in jsdom).

Running a REAL bpmn-js Modeler under jsdom needs an SVG-geometry polyfill (getBBox, SVGMatrix global, transform.baseVal list, createSVGMatrix/Transform, CSS.escape) — measurement-only, does not touch the command stack under test. Kept local to escalation-branch-undo.test.js; reusable pattern for future canvas tests.
